text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto met British Prime Minister John Major during an overnight stay at London before leaving for New York.
- An afghan national was killed and another wounded when Pakistani border security personnel fired on a mob of Afghan nationals at Pakistan-Afghan border at Torkham.
- A joint-petition filed by wives of Murtaza Bhutto and his aide Ashiq Hussain Jatio in the High Court of Sindh province was fixed for hearing on October 7.
- Cotton output this year will reach 10 million bales (375-lb each) despite a recent pest flare up, an official said.

- Pakistani officials on Saturday had their first meetings with officials of the International Monetary Fund in which Pakistan presented a policy package aimed at convincing IMF for resumption of a new structural adjustment facility.
- A number of cooking oil manufacturers have shut their mills after the state-run Utiltity Stores Corporation didnot lift stocks it had committed to purchase, sources said.
- The government has relieved on MOnday 11 judges and regularised 29 hudges of high court following March 20 judgement of the supre Court.

- Police have arrested an Indian High Commission official in Islamabad on the charges of spying and a map of sensitive military installations in Pakistan alongwith some other important documents were recovered from his possession.
- The government is seeking reports on corrupt officials.
